messages:
maria: quick one — we started seeing 401s from the hosted API when running in our Windows CI runner. header looks fine locally. suspect env var encoding/trailing chars? :thinking:
aj: do you have an example of how you're building the auth header? windows often adds CRLF or a BOM when secrets are written out by some actions
maria: in GH actions we write to a file then load into env. building header in node like: `const hdr = 'Basic ' + Buffer.from(process.env.API_KEY + ':').toString('base64')` — same code works on macOS.
aj: two quick checks: 1) echo the bytes to see stray chars: `printf "%s" "$API_KEY" | xxd` (or on windows `Get-Content secret.txt -AsByteStream`). 2) trim CR/LF and BOM: `apiKey.replace(/^\uFEFF|\r|\n/g, '')`.
sam: also note difference between browsers/deno and node base64 helpers — btoa in browser will throw on unicode, Buffer in node is binary-safe. For deno/edge use `btoa(unescape(encodeURIComponent(key)))` or Deno.core ops.
maria: ran the xxd — shows 0xef 0xbb 0xbf at start (BOM). how did that get there? our pipeline step saved the key from a secret file created by some Windows step.
aj: yep BOM. easiest fix is to sanitize right after reading: `const key = fs.readFileSync('/tmp/secret.txt', 'utf8').replace(/^\uFEFF/, '').trim()` then build the header. If you can't change the writer, always sanitize consumer side.
maria: quick test — updated to sanitize and re-run, headers now accept and no more 401s. thanks! :tada:
sam: small follow-up: for streaming clients, we saw weird broken-chunk errors when auth header had trailing newline. The server treats header mismatch as auth failure mid-stream and kills connection — so sanitize before any keepalive.
aj: and for retries, make sure your retry middleware doesn't re-use a stale header variable if you mutate env in process — better to compute header per-request or cache a sanitized value immutably.
maria: thanks — will patch our node client and add a tiny test that writes BOM-prefixed secret and asserts client strips it.
devx-bot: Reminder: small PRs fixing infra tests should target branch `ci/patch-quickfix` and include a changelog line.
